verses.commentary: Gather together, shameful nation. The Hebrew qoshesu suggests collecting stubble or straw, worthless material. Judah has become refuse. Yet even refuse is called to assemble before judgment falls.
Before the decree takes effect, before that day passes like chaff, before fierce anger arrives. Triple 'before' creates urgency. A window remains open, but not for long. Time is running out.

Seek the Lord, seek righteousness, seek humility. The humble of the land who do his commands. Perhaps (ulay) you will be sheltered. No guarantee, only possibility. Grace is not presumptuous. Seek while seeking is possible.

Oracles against nations begin. Gaza abandoned, Ashkelon ruined, Ashdod emptied at midday, Ekron uprooted. Four Philistine cities. Wordplay: Gaza (azzah) becomes azuvah (abandoned), Ekron (eqron) becomes teaqer (uprooted). Judgment has linguistic precision.

Woe to the Kerethites (Cretans who settled in Philistia). The word of the Lord is against Canaan. I will destroy you until none remains. Total elimination announced. Ancient enemies of Israel face final reckoning.
The seacoast becomes pasture land. Shepherds' wells, sheep pens. Cities become rural wilderness. Urban civilization replaced by agrarian simplicity. Reversal of development.
The remnant of Judah inherits Philistine territory. They pasture flocks, rest in Ashkelon's houses. The Lord their God cares for them, restores their fortunes. Enemy territory becomes inheritance.
God has heard Moab's insults and Ammon's taunts. They mocked God's people and threatened their land. Nations across the Jordan, descended from Lot. Family contempt compounds the offense.

Solemn oath: as I live, declares the Lord. Moab becomes like Sodom, Ammon like Gomorrah. Weeds, salt pits, wasteland forever. Israel's remnant plunders them, survivors inherit. Lot's descendants meet Lot's neighbors' fate.
This is what they get for their pride. Insulting and mocking the people of the Lord of hosts. Pride goes before destruction. Mockery rebounds. What they directed at Israel returns upon them.
The Lord will be awesome (terrifying) to them when he destroys all earth's gods. Distant nations will worship him, each in their own land. Universal recognition emerges from universal judgment.
Cush (Ethiopia/Nubia) also slain by God's sword. The distant south included in judgment. No geography escapes. God's reach extends to earth's limits.
His hand stretches against the north. Assyria destroyed, Nineveh desolate and dry as desert. The superpower of the age falls. What seems invincible is vulnerable to divine decree.

Flocks lie down in Nineveh. Every creature inhabits it. Desert owl and screech owl roost on columns. Hooting echoes through windows. Rubble fills doorways, cedar beams exposed. The great city becomes animal habitat. Ruins replace splendor.

The carefree city that lived in security, saying 'I am, and there is no one else.' Divine self designation ('I am') mocked. Now a ruin, a lair for beasts. Passersby scoff and shake fists. Pride's end is contempt.
